title: Bidirectional Dijkstra to the Bridge in Alfama!
description: Watch Bidirectional Dijkstra slice through Alfama’s real street-style graph, expanding from both start and goal at once. The visualization shows how two frontiers meet sooner to find the shortest path efficiently.
ig_caption:
🚦✨ **Bidirectional Dijkstra in Lisbon’s Alfama** ✨🚦

This reel visualizes **Bidirectional Dijkstra**: instead of running one Dijkstra search from start to finish, we run **two coordinated priority queues**—one forward from the source and one backward from the destination—until the explored regions overlap.

🧠 **Graph theory moment:** Treat the street network as a weighted graph (nodes = intersections, edges = streets with costs like distance/time). Each side maintains a frontier ordered by cumulative cost, so when the forward and backward searches meet, we can reconstruct the shortest path with significantly fewer expansions than classic single-source Dijkstra—especially on large, sparse real-world maps.

📍From winding alleys to hillier segments, the algorithm adapts to varying edge weights while still guaranteeing optimality under non-negative costs.
